title: Federated Micro-Frontend Host Shell with Module Federation, Shared Runtime State & Error Boundaries
problem: Monolithic enterprise frontend applications suffer from slow continuous integration build cycles, coupled release cadences, and brittle global state dependencies across distributed product teams. Standard iframe-based embedding creates degraded user experiences with clunky cross-window communication and duplicated vendor bundles. This project builds a federated micro-frontend host architecture in React, TypeScript, and Webpack 5 Module Federation. The host shell dynamically loads isolated remote micro-applications at runtime, coordinates shared singleton dependencies to prevent duplicate bundle downloads, implements a typed cross-app event bus for decoupled state synchronization, and isolates remote crashes using React error boundaries.

use_cases.title: Enterprise Cloud Console Multi-Team Dashboard
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise SaaS companies with autonomous product teams need a centralized administrative console where teams deploy services independently without rebuilding the host shell.
use_cases.second_sentence: The host shell dynamically imports remote micro-apps for billing, usage analytics, and identity management, rendering a unified user interface while maintaining decoupled release pipelines.

use_cases.title: Digital Banking Customer Self-Service Portal
use_cases.first_sentence: Financial institutions with strict compliance boundaries require isolated deployment surfaces for payment processing, loan applications, and investment accounts.
use_cases.second_sentence: The shell manages user authentication and global layout tokens, delegating account workflows to independent remote applications that load on-demand without cross-domain iframe issues.

use_cases.title: Healthcare Provider Clinic Management Platform
use_cases.first_sentence: Hospital networks deploying patient scheduling, clinical charting, and pharmacy modules need resilient frontends where failures in auxiliary modules do not crash critical patient care views.
use_cases.second_sentence: The architecture isolates remote child applications behind resilient error boundary fallbacks, ensuring clinicians can record vitals even if an external billing micro-frontend fails to load.

hard_parts: Configuring Webpack 5 Module Federation with shared singleton runtime dependencies (React, React-DOM, UI tokens) to eliminate bundle duplication
Designing a typed, framework-agnostic custom event bus allowing bidirectional communication between micro-frontends without tight coupling
Implementing resilient error boundaries and skeleton placeholders that prevent unresponsive remote bundles from blank-screening the host application
Isolating CSS namespaces using Tailwind prefixing and CSS modules to prevent remote child styles from overriding host design systems
screener_signals: Clean TypeScript codebase cleanly separating the host shell container, remote micro-apps, and shared contracts library
Automated bundle analysis report confirming shared vendor chunk singletons and sub-120KB initial host shell payload size
Anti-fake verification script dynamically registering a novel remote micro-app at runtime and verifying the host shell imports and renders it without rebuilding

architecture.data_flow: The user loads the host shell in the browser; the shell initialises the shared React singleton and global theme context; as the user navigates to an application route, the Module Federation runtime requests the target remoteEntry.js script from its CDN endpoint; if the network call succeeds, the remote component mounts seamlessly inside the shell layout; cross-app interactions (such as updating active workspace or currency) publish typed events through the shared event bus; if a remote fails to load or encounters a runtime exception, the error boundary renders a fallback retry card while maintaining full host shell operability.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Webpack singleton sharing configuration throwing strict version mismatch warnings; TypeScript interface contracts validating event bus payloads.

riskiest_component.name: React Runtime Version Conflicts Between Host and Remotes
riskiest_component.mitigation: Configure Webpack ModuleFederationPlugin shared configuration with singleton: true and strictVersion: false.
riskiest_component.fallback: Enforce peerDependencies lockfile pinning identical React versions across all micro-app packages.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a federated micro-frontend host shell in React/TypeScript with Webpack 5 Module Federation, shared singletons, and error boundaries.
worksheet.q2: Target users: frontend platform engineers, web architects, and enterprise UI developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: enterprise cloud console dashboards, digital banking portals, and clinical hospital management platforms.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: Webpack Module Federation singleton sharing, cross-app typed event bus coordination, error boundary isolation, and CSS namespace encapsulation.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: host shell Webpack config, 2 remote micro-app source trees, and event contract schemas. Synthetic mock data only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local static HTTP servers.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: React runtime version conflicts. Fallback: singleton: true in ModuleFederationPlugin and peerDependencies lockfile.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static hardcoded component imports. Anti-fake check 5 serves dynamic unobserved remote on local port, asserts runtime mount.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local development servers and mock telemetry only, zero sensitive enterprise data.
